mainTopic: Moving פסח meat out of its place, the boundaries of inside and outside, and the holiness of gateways and roofs
overview: The גמרא first learns from the word ״חוּצָה״ that it is forbidden to move קרבן פסח meat from one חבורה to another. רבי אמי rules that a person is liable only once he puts the meat down, because the Torah's word הוצאה matches carrying on שבת, which needs both עקירה and הנחה. רבי אבא בר ממל challenges this from the burned inner offerings. He then answers himself: those offerings were being dragged on the ground, so they count as already placed. A new משנה teaches how to cut off the part of a פסח limb that went outside without breaking a bone. It also defines the boundary: the doorway divides inside from outside, and windows and the thickness of the wall count as inside. The גמרא notes that רב applies the doorway rule to prayer, which disagrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי. It then resolves a contradiction in the משנה about the doorway itself: doorways of the עזרה count as inside, and doorways of ירושלים count as outside. Two statements of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק about מצורעים support this. Finally, רב rules that roofs and upper stories were not sanctified, and the גמרא challenges him from his own saying about the loud הלל on the roofs. That challenge is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Where do we learn the ban on moving the meat between groups?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that moving קרבן פסח meat from one חבורה to another is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that it is forbidden to take the meat from one group to another group?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a source question. It is setting up the next step, where a ברייתא will give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah clearly forbids taking the meat out of the house. The question is whether the ban also covers moving it between two groups who are eating in the same house. Something in the verse must teach that.

keyTerms.meaning: A group registered together to eat one קרבן פסח

phrases.english: From group to group — from where do we know it is forbidden?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source forbidding the transfer of פסח meat between groups, even within one house.

steps.title: The word ״חוצה״ includes moving the meat between groups
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word ״חוּצָה״ that taking the meat anywhere outside its eating place, including to another group, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall not carry any of the meat out of the house to the outside.' From this I only know that moving it from house to house is forbidden. How do I know that moving it from group to group is forbidden too? The verse says 'to the outside', meaning outside the place where it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads the extra word ״חוּצָה״ as widening the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from the house' alone would only cover moving the meat out of a building. The extra word 'outside' is read as 'outside its eating place'. Each group's spot counts as its own eating place, so moving the meat to another group is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from the plain verse)

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'You shall not carry out of the house'
any of the meat to the outside'
I only know that moving it from house to house is forbidden
from where do we know it is forbidden from group to group?
The verse says: 'to the outside'
meaning outside the place where it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word ״חוּצָה״ means 'outside its eating place', which includes another group's place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next discussion. Once moving the meat counts as a forbidden 'carrying out', the גמרא asks exactly when the violation happens.

steps.title: No liability until the meat is put down, just like carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that a person who moves פסח meat between groups is liable only once he puts it down. He compares this to הוצאה on שבת, which needs both עקירה and הנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: One who carries פסח meat from one group to another is not liable until he puts it down. The Torah uses the word 'carrying out' here, as it does for שבת. On שבת a person is not liable until he both lifts and places. Here too, he is not liable until he both lifts and places.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives a new rule about when the sin happens: only after the meat is set down. He backs it up with a comparison to שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's word for this ban is 'תוציא', the same root as the שבת labor of הוצאה. On שבת, carrying only counts when you lift from one place and set down in another. So רבי אמי says lifting the meat alone, or just walking it over, is not enough. It must be placed at the second group.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out (also the name of the שבת labor)
Lifting the object from its place
Setting the object down in its new place

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
One who carries Paschal meat from group to group
is not liable until he places it down.
'Carrying out' is written about it, just as with Shabbat:

phrases.aramaic: מָה שַׁבָּת — עַד דְּעָבֵד עֲקִירָה וְהַנָּחָה,
phrases.english: just as on Shabbat, one is not liable until he does lifting and placing,

phrases.aramaic: אַף הָכָא נָמֵי — עַד דְּעָבֵד עֲקִירָה וְהַנָּחָה.
phrases.english: so too here, not until he does lifting and placing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ban from step 2 and defines when it is violated
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for moving פסח meat requires both עקירה and הנחה, based on the shared word הוצאה with שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי is not saying moving the meat is allowed. He is only saying the full punishable sin is completed when the meat is set down.

steps.title: Challenge: the carriers of burned offerings become impure just by stepping out
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל challenges רבי אמי from the burned inner offerings. Those carriers become impure as soon as they leave the עזרה, even though nothing was set down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל objected: If they were carrying the offerings on poles, and the people in front had gone out past the wall of the עזרה while the people in back had not, the ones in front make their clothes impure and the ones in back do not. But the offering was not placed down! (So why does it already count as taken out?)
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל attacks רבי אמי's rule. He brings a case where 'going out' counts right away, without any placing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The carriers of פרים ושעירים הנשרפים become impure once the offering is taken out of the עזרה. The ruling makes the front carriers impure the moment they cross the wall, while the offering is still hanging on poles. That suggests 'carrying out' is complete without הנחה, which contradicts רבי אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: The wall of the Temple courtyard
But it was not set down!

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel raised an objection:
If they were carrying them on poles,
and those in front went out past the wall of the courtyard
while those in back had not gone out,
those in front make their garments impure
and those in back do not make their garments impure.
But it has not been set down!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אמי's requirement of הנחה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's rule that 'carrying out' requires הנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With the burned offerings, 'going out' takes effect the moment the carriers cross the wall while the offering is still on poles. So 'carrying out' should not need placing.

steps.title: Answer: the offerings were being dragged on the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל answers his own challenge. The case is one where the offerings were dragged along the ground, so they count as already set down.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection and he himself answered it: the case is where they were dragging the offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The same רבי אבא בר ממל resolves his own question. The ברייתא is about offerings dragged along the ground, not lifted high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the offering is being dragged, it is resting on the ground the whole time. Once part of it passes the wall, it is already lying outside, and that counts as הנחה. So the case fits רבי אמי's rule, and his requirement of הנחה stands.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He asked it and he answered it himself

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אמי, taking פסח meat to another חבורה is learned from ״חוּצָה״. Like שבת carrying, it needs both עקירה and הנחה. The burned-offerings case does not disprove this, because the offerings were dragged on the ground and so were already 'placed'.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ,
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
It refers to offerings being dragged.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 4 and defends רבי אמי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the offerings were dragged, not lifted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The offerings were lifted on poles, so leaving the courtyard happened without placing
steps.terutzMaskana: Dragged offerings rest on the ground, so crossing the wall already counts as הנחה. רבי אמי's rule stands.

steps.title: Cutting off the part of a limb that went outside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if part of a limb of the פסח left its permitted area, you cut the meat down to the bone, peel the meat to the joint, and separate at the joint. For other קדשים you may chop through the bone with a hatchet.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If part of a limb went out of its permitted area, he cuts the meat until he reaches the bone. Then he peels the meat back until he reaches the joint, and cuts there. But with other sacrifices, he may chop it off with a hatchet, because the ban on breaking a bone does not apply to them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It explains what to do when part of a piece of פסח meat went out of bounds and became forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part that went out is forbidden, but the part still inside is fine, so you must separate them. With the פסח you may not break a bone (שבירת העצם), so you cannot just chop through. You cut the meat down to the bone, peel it back to the natural joint, and separate there. Other sacrifices have no such ban, so a hatchet is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb or body part of the animal
Peels (the meat away from the bone)
A joint, where two bones naturally meet
The ban on breaking a bone of the קרבן פסח

steps.confusionAlert: The peeling procedure is NOT because the meat inside is forbidden. The inside part is fully permitted. The whole careful process exists only to avoid breaking a bone of the פסח.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
A limb, part of which went out (of its boundary)
he cuts (the meat) until he reaches the bone
phrases.notes: He cuts at the border line between the inside and outside parts.

phrases.english: and peels (the meat off) until he reaches the joint
and (then) cuts (at the joint)
But with (other) sacrifices
he chops it off with a hatchet
since the ban on breaking a bone does not apply to it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It continues the theme of פסח meat leaving its permitted place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separate the part of a פסח limb that went out by cutting to the bone and peeling to the joint, never breaking a bone. Other קדשים may be chopped with a hatchet.

steps.title: Where inside ends and outside begins
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines the boundary. Inside the doorway is inside, outside the doorway is outside, and the windows and the thickness of the wall count as inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the doorway inward is like inside. From the doorway outward is like outside. The windows and the thickness of the wall are like inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now defines exactly where the boundary line is, so we know when meat has gone out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doorway is the dividing line between inside and outside. The windows and the thick part of the wall are treated as inside. So meat resting in a window or within the wall's width has not yet left. Notice that the משנה describes the areas on either side of the doorway but does not say directly where the doorway space itself belongs. This gap will matter in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The doorway, the spot where the door closes

phrases.english: From the doorway inward
is like inside
from the doorway outward
is like outside
The windows and the thickness of the wall
are like inside

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the boundary that step 6 assumed (what counts as the limb having gone out).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doorway divides inside from outside. Windows and the wall's thickness count as inside.

steps.title: רב applies the doorway rule to prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the same doorway boundary applies to prayer. Someone standing outside the doorway is not counted together with those praying inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: And the same is true for prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by taking the משנה's doorway boundary and applying it to תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the פסח, the doorway decides whether meat is inside or outside. רב says the doorway also decides whether a person is part of the praying group inside. So someone beyond the doorway is considered outside and does not join them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said
And likewise for prayer
phrases.notes: One outside the doorway is not joined with those praying inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב וְכֵן לִתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the boundary rule of step 7 to a new area, prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doorway boundary also decides who is included with a praying group.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי disagrees: no barrier blocks prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב argues with רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said that even an iron wall does not separate Israel from their Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי. For רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Even a wall of iron does not separate between Israel and their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב's view is disputed. It quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי, who holds that walls do not matter at all for prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, a doorway can separate a person from the praying group. According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, no physical barrier matters for prayer, not even iron, because prayer reaches ה׳ regardless. So someone outside still counts with those inside.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
Even a barrier of iron
does not separate
between Israel and their Father in Heaven

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב's prayer rule from step 8 is disputed. It is not a refutation, just a noted disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, no physical barrier separates a person from the praying congregation.

steps.title: The משנה contradicts itself about the doorway space
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and finds a contradiction. The first clause implies the doorway itself is outside, but the second clause implies it is inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is difficult. You said: from the doorway inward is like inside. That implies the doorway itself is like outside. Now say the next clause: from the doorway outward is like outside. That implies the doorway itself is like inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and challenges it from within. It reads each half by inference and shows the two halves clash about the doorway space itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "From the doorway inward" suggests that only what is past the doorway counts as inside, so the doorway itself is outside. "From the doorway outward" suggests that only what is beyond the doorway counts as outside, so the doorway itself is inside. Both inferences cannot be true, so the גמרא needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult (the text contradicts itself)
The first clause (implied here as the source of the first inference)

steps.confusionAlert: Neither clause openly mentions the doorway space itself. Both rulings about it are inferences ("הא" = which implies). The contradiction comes from comparing those two inferences.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult
You said
from the doorway inward is like inside
which implies the doorway itself is like outside
Now say the latter clause
from the doorway outward is like outside
which implies the doorway itself is like inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the prayer discussion and returns to the wording of the משנה in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's boundary rule (step 7): the status of the doorway space itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inferences from the first and second clauses give opposite statuses to the doorway itself (outside versus inside). That is an internal contradiction.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer will decide which part of the doorway counts as inside, and that tells us exactly when פסח meat has left its permitted place.

steps.title: The two clauses refer to two different kinds of gates
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction disappears once we see that the two clauses of the משנה are talking about different gates. The doorways of the עזרה count as inside, and the doorways of ירושלים count as outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, the clause is talking about the gates of the עזרה. There, the clause is talking about the gates of ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 10. Each clause of the משנה is speaking about a different set of gates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second clause, where the doorway counts as inside, is about the gates of the עזרה. The first clause, where the doorway counts as outside, is about the gates of ירושלים. Each clause is now consistent because it describes a different place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening words of an answer
Here... there; this splits two sources into two different cases
The gates of the Temple courtyard
The gates of the city of Jerusalem

steps.confusionAlert: The first כאן (עזרה) actually matches the second clause of the משנה, and the second כאן (ירושלים) matches the first clause. Do not line them up by order.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is about the gates of the Temple courtyard,
phrases.notes: Here the doorway counts as inside.

phrases.english: there, it is about the gates of Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: Here the doorway counts as outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן — בְּשַׁעֲרֵי עֲזָרָה, כָּאן — בְּשַׁעֲרֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each clause refers to a different location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses seemed to describe the same doorway, so they appeared to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doorways of the עזרה gates are inside. Doorways of the ירושלים gates are outside.

steps.title: Why the gateways of ירושלים were left unsanctified
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק explains that the gateways of ירושלים were left unsanctified. This let מצורעים, who may not enter the city, shelter under them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: Why were the gates of ירושלים not sanctified? Because מצורעים shelter under them. In the sun they shelter from the sun, and in the rain they shelter from the rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to support its answer. That source confirms that the gateways of ירושלים really are considered outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע is not allowed inside ירושלים. If the gateways were holy, a מצורע could not stand there. They were left unsanctified on purpose so that מצורעים could find shelter. This supports the claim that the ירושלים doorway counts as outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Were sanctified, meaning given holy status
People with צרעת (a spiritual skin affliction), who may not enter holy areas

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נִתְקַדְּשׁוּ שַׁעֲרֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם?
phrases.english: Why were the gates of Jerusalem not sanctified?
Because lepers shelter under them,
in the sun, from the sun,
and in the rain, from the rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ירושלים half of the answer in Step 11
steps.raayaObject: The doorways of the ירושלים gates count as outside
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק: the gates of ירושלים were not sanctified so that מצורעים could shelter there

steps.title: Why only שער נקנור of the עזרה was left unsanctified
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק also explains that שער נקנור was left unsanctified so that מצורעים could stand there for their purification. This implies that the other gates of the עזרה were sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: Why was שער נקנור not sanctified? Because מצורעים stand there and put their thumbs inside the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement from the same אמורא supports the עזרה half of the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healed מצורע stands at שער נקנור and reaches his thumbs into the עזרה so that blood from his offering can be placed on them. A special reason was needed to leave this one gate unsanctified. That shows the normal rule is that the gateways of the עזרה are sanctified, which means they count as inside.

keyTerms.meaning: The Nicanor Gate, the main eastern gate into the עזרה
Their thumbs, where blood from the purification offering is placed

steps.whatToRemember: The rule: doorways of the עזרה are holy (inside), except שער נקנור. Doorways of ירושלים are not holy (outside). Both exceptions exist so that מצורעים can be accommodated.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נִתְקַדְּשָׁה שַׁעַר נִקָּנוֹר?
phrases.english: Why was the Nicanor Gate not sanctified?
Because lepers stand there
and put their thumbs inside.
phrases.notes: The thumbs go into the עזרה so that blood from the offering can be placed on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporting statement, this time for the עזרה half of the answer
steps.raayaObject: The doorways of the עזרה gates count as inside
steps.raayaSupportSource: Only שער נקנור needed a special reason to be left unsanctified, so the other עזרה gates were sanctified

steps.title: רב rules that roofs and upper stories were not sanctified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about windows and wall thickness. רב adds that roofs and upper stories did not receive holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the windows and the thickness of the wall, etc. רב said: Roofs and upper stories were not sanctified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. It then brings רב's ruling that roofs and upper stories are not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counted windows and wall thickness as inside. רב sets a limit on that. Anything above, such as roofs and upper rooms, did not receive the holiness of the area below. This applies both to the עזרה and to ירושלים.

phrases.english: The windows and the thickness of the wall, etc.
Rav said: Roofs and upper stories
were not sanctified.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחַלּוֹנוֹת וָעוֹבִי הַחוֹמָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gates discussion and moves to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roofs and upper stories did not receive the holiness of the עזרה or of ירושלים.

steps.title: רב's own saying suggests the פסח was eaten on rooftops
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with his own saying in the name of רבי חייא. The הלל was so loud it seemed to split the roofs, which implies people ate the פסח up on the roofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But didn't רב say in the name of רבי חייא: 'The פסח is the size of an olive, and the הלל breaks the roofs'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling from Step 14 using another statement of רב himself. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So many people shared each פסח that each person got only a כזית, and their הלל sounded like it was splitting the roofs. That suggests people were eating on the roofs. The פסח may only be eaten inside ירושלים, so the roofs must have had the holiness of ירושלים. That contradicts רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so?; the opening word of a challenge
The הלל, songs of praise said while eating the פסח

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav say in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
"The Paschal lamb is the size of an olive,"
phrases.notes: So many people were registered on each lamb that each person got only a כזית.

phrases.english: "and the Hallel breaks the roofs."
phrases.notes: This implies people were eating up on the roofs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that roofs were not sanctified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The saying implies people ate the פסח on roofs in ירושלים. The פסח may only be eaten within ירושלים. Therefore the roofs must have had the city's holiness.
